### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **3** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json efcbac73cc58510278b970949ac3b65cb9712815` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `560621f0f609f75b4f957a141adad95e94de103b` — the merge of head `27331626c8f044e5d77394a4dc71f3d3ac61609a` into base `efcbac73cc58510278b970949ac3b65cb9712815`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 560621f0f609f75b4f957a141adad95e94de103b && git checkout 560621f0f609f75b4f957a141adad95e94de103b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin efcbac73cc58510278b970949ac3b65cb9712815 27331626c8f044e5d77394a4dc71f3d3ac61609a && git checkout -B drift-repro efcbac73cc58510278b970949ac3b65cb9712815 && git merge --no-ff 27331626c8f044e5d77394a4dc71f3d3ac61609a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json efcbac73cc58510278b970949ac3b65cb9712815
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `27331626c8f044e5d77394a4dc71f3d3ac61609a`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #22599 (body and all 4 comments: triage 6093534577, unlock 6107817243, claim 6108442214, os-dev-report 6108899708), PR #22830 (body, 3-file list, net diff at the head), and the head's check-runs (polled at 12:19Z, 12:22Z and 12:24Z). Context read on `origin/main` `b7cd1af9df` (the commit the claim and the dev read): `packages/verify/src/handle.ts` (its blob `6641851314` is the diff's base blob), `packages/verify/src/index.ts`, both verify tsconfigs, `packages/verify/package.json`, `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` (the `delete` and `update` declarations and the by-id delete body), `packages/objectql/src/verb-hook-result-shape.ts`, `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`, `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `.changeset/pre.json`, `.changeset/config.json`, and the `Check Changeset` job in `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml`.

### ① Derived judgments

The diff touches three files, all inside the claim's declared file surface (`handle.ts`, one type test in `packages/verify`, one `.changeset/22599-*.md`), and no engine file. Every surface change it implies, named:

1. **`VerifyHandle.hooks.run`, the person overload (`opts: AsUser`): the `delete` answer narrows from a Promise of `EngineRow` to a Promise of `HookWriteAnswer` of `Op`, which for `Op = 'delete'` is `EngineDeleteAnswer`, that is `Awaited` of `ReturnType` of `ObjectQL['delete']`, which the engine declares as a Promise of `boolean | number` (engine.ts line 18145 on `origin/main`).** Right. This is a published-surface narrowing: a consumer may do less with the answer (a field read is now a compile error), and the accept set of the call is unchanged. It is the card's direction A, taken as the triage worded it.
2. **The system overload (`opts: AsSystem`, the #22301 one): the same narrowing.** Right. The card named both callers, and the base on `origin/main` already carries the #22301 overload, so the ordering constraint (behind #22301) held at claim.
3. **Both overloads become generic over `Op extends 'insert' | 'update' | 'delete'`, with `operation: Op`.** Right, and it moves no accept set: a `string`-typed operation was refused before and is refused now; the three literals and their union were accepted before and are accepted now. The dev's measurement that split overloads would refuse a union-typed operation (TS2769) is the correct reason to keep one generic overload per caller kind: splitting would have narrowed the accept set, which the card did not order.
4. **A call whose operation is the union type now resolves with `EngineRow | boolean | number` instead of `EngineRow`.** Right, and correctly declared as part of the same narrowing (`HookWriteAnswer` is distributive over a naked type parameter). No in-repo call site passes a non-literal operation (grep on `origin/main`: every `hooks.run(` call passes a literal), so nothing in the repo moves; the new test pins the union resolution.
5. **`insert` and `update` answers stay `EngineRow` for both callers.** Right, unchanged, and pinned by the test for all four combinations.
6. **No new public export.** Right. `EngineDeleteAnswer` and `HookWriteAnswer` are module-local aliases (no `export`), `packages/verify/src/index.ts` re-exports a named list (not `export *`), and the `AutomationCondition` alias in the same file is the precedent for an unexported alias that the published d.ts inlines as a local declaration. The only new type-level reference the published d.ts gains is `ObjectQL` from `@objectstack/objectql`, already imported as a type in `handle.ts` and a declared runtime dependency of the package.
7. **Runtime: nothing moves.** Right. The implementation hunk changes comment lines only; each `case` still returns the engine call unchanged. `hooks.updateWhere`, `seed`, `rows` and every other member are untouched.
8. **The whole-verb declaration (`boolean | number`) rather than a hand-written `boolean` satisfies direction A.** Right, on two readings. (a) The ruling's letter: the triage said "if the engine publishes a declared return type for a by-id delete, read that one type, not a hand-written copy". The engine publishes exactly one declared return type for `delete`, covering the by-id and predicate paths, and no separate by-id type; reading it off `ObjectQL['delete']` is that instruction followed literally, and a plain `boolean` would be the hand-written copy it forbade. (b) The runtime envelope: the by-id branch returns `hookContext.result` after `afterDelete` dispatch, and the engine's own `isDeleteResultShape` admits any `boolean` or `number` there, so an `afterDelete` hook may lawfully substitute a count on a by-id delete; `boolean | number` is therefore what the door can answer, and `true` is what it ordinarily answers. The cost is small and stated in the changeset: a consumer who wants `boolean` narrows.
9. **The shipped docblocks are accurate.** The new `EngineDeleteAnswer` docblock says a row that is not there is refused before the driver runs: the engine's by-id delete reads the pre-image and throws `recordNotFoundError` before `driver.delete` (engine.ts, by-id branch), so that holds. The `hooks.run` docblock now says what each write resolves with, and that a test needing the deleted row reads it before the delete. One observation, not a defect: the docblock explains the `number` arm as the predicate delete's count and does not mention the hook-substitution path on a by-id delete; the PR body does. Nothing false ships.
10. **The type test is in the program that judges it.** `tsconfig.test.json` includes `src/**/*`; `tsconfig.json` excludes `**/*.test.ts`; `check:test-typecheck` runs inside `pnpm --filter @objectstack/verify typecheck`. The reverse check the dev reports (TS2344 on the delete and union lines, TS2554 on the `not.toHaveProperty('id')` lines under the old annotation, with insert and update staying green) is the right shape for a type test that can fail. The card asked for a type pin, which this is; a runtime assertion of the `true` answer in an existing boot test would be a welcome addition, not a condition.

Wrong or missing: nothing found.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset:** `.changeset/22599-verify-hooks-run-delete-answer.md`, `@objectstack/verify` `minor`, title `fix(verify)!:`, a **BREAKING** banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, and one ADR-0087 marker. Not `skip-changeset`, correctly: the diff moves a published type on a released package.
- **Level:** `minor` matches what the diff publishes. The change is a breaking narrowing of a published TypeScript surface with no runtime change, which `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` describes in its own level-axis text as "a BREAKING change; during the launch window it ships `minor`", and which the post-22080 narrowings on `main` (22149, 22168, 22345) graded the same way. Two facts the record states for the adopting seat: `.changeset/pre.json` is in pre mode (tag `next`), where the no-major guard stands aside, so `major` would also have been admitted but is not required; and because every published package is in the fixed group and the v18 opener (22080) already holds a pending `major`, the level moves no version on its own, so the carriers of breaking-ness are the banner, the bang and the ADR-0087 disposition, all present.
- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`:** right. The diff adds no key on a published payload and no public export (the widening question is honestly `no`), and the `narrowing` arm declares the break. The claim comment, the PR body and the changeset carry the same line.
- **ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (runtime-interface-only packages/verify/src/handle.ts#VerifyHandle)`:** consistent with the diff, and I re-verified the category's four predicates by reading rather than by trusting the gate: (1) `handle.ts` exists at the head and exports `interface VerifyHandle`; (2) `handle.ts` is not a metadata surface (not a Zod file, not under spec contracts, not an object definition); (3) the interface is not a Zod projection; (4) no metadata-surface file on `origin/main` references `VerifyHandle` (grep over `*.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/contracts`, object definitions: zero hits). The marker's closing of the other categories is honest: the package publishes; no ADR-0087 id covers a test handle's return type and none is added; `EngineRow` is a concrete named type at the base, so `type-surface-only` predicate 4 refuses it. The gate's CI verdict is the `Check Changeset` check-run (success at 12:11:36Z), whose job runs `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base MERGE_BASE` and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base MERGE_BASE`.
- **Migration text for an upgrading TypeScript author:** present in substance. The body states the from (a Promise of `EngineRow`), the to (`boolean | number`, read off `ObjectQL['delete']`, `true` for a by-id delete), and the one-line fix (`expect(await stack.hooks.run(object, 'delete', { id }, opts)).toBe(true)`, and read the row with `stack.rows` before the delete if the test needs it). It is prose rather than a FROM-arrow-TO label, and that is the only form available: `runtime-interface-only` inherits the no-migration-prescription refusal (an arrow label or a migration-framed heading would red the gate), `type-surface-only` is closed on its predicate 4, and `registered` would put a TypeScript-only surface in the ledger that `objectstack migrate meta` cannot reach. The landed 22345 changeset is the same shape. I checked the body against the detector's own patterns: no operand-arrow-operand line, no migration-framed heading, no table, no retirement line.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev `open_questions`: none declared. Every dev deviation, out-of-scope finding and acceptance note, answered or escalated:

1. **Migration text in prose, not a FROM-arrow-TO label** (dev deviation 1, PR body note): answered in ② above. Accepted: the content the order asked for is there, and the label form is refused by every category this change can honestly claim.
2. **Generic overloads instead of split overloads** (dev deviation 2): answered in ① item 3. Right: the generic form keeps the accept set the card did not order narrowed and still types the answer per operation; the union resolution is pinned.
3. **Whole-verb `boolean | number` rather than a plain `boolean`** (dev deviation 3): answered in ① item 8. Right by the triage's own wording and by the engine's by-id branch; the flip to a plain `boolean` the dev offered is not taken.
4. **Three PID files left at the dev container's filesystem root** (dev deviation 4): outside this record's inputs and outside the repository; nothing in the diff. Relayed to the adopting seat as container hygiene needing a person's rm on that container; not a condition on this PR.
5. **One-commit fetch to deepen the shallow clone for a gate's pinned control** (dev deviation 5): local and additive; no effect on the diff. Nothing for the record.
6. **`update` has the same class of gap** (dev out-of-scope finding): escalated to the adopting seat as a candidate class (b) card for the same lane, not this PR's. On `origin/main` the engine's `update` declares a Promise of `Record` of string to any `| number | null` (engine.ts line 15166), while `hooks.run` keeps declaring `EngineRow` for `update`; the `null` arm (a by-id write whose readback leaves the caller's row scope) is reachable through this door for a person caller, the `number` arm is not (the door never takes the predicate path). Reach is unmeasured; the claim's file surface named the delete overloads only, so leaving it out was right.
7. **`packages/verify/README.md` unchanged** (PR acceptance note): answered. Its one delete call reads no answer; nothing it says is false.
8. **Check-runs on the head, last read at 12:24Z:** 33 runs, 30 completed (27 `success`, 3 `skipped` by design: Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke opt-in) and 3 still `in_progress`: Lint & Repo Gates, Test Core (1/6), Test Core (2/6). An in-progress run is not green and this record does not call it so; the adopting seat reads their conclusions before landing. Of the completed ones, the gate verdicts this review leans on are `Check Changeset` (ADR-0087 disposition and no-major), `Type Check · workspace` (the package typecheck that compiles the new type test), `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · source gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core`, `Dogfood Verify CLI` and the three Dogfood Regression Gate shards, all `success`. The full `pnpm lint` the dev ran only as a proven narrowing is the `Lint & Repo Gates` run's business.
